title: WPMS/1728/2020 of SWAMI UMA BHARTI Vs NATIONAL HIGHWAY AUTHORITY OF INDIA

paras.text:
Judgment Reserved on : 02.09.2021
 Judgment Delivered on : 30.09.2021
IN HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No.1728 of 2020 (M/S)
Swami Uma Bharti & another .....Petitioners
Vs.
National Highway Authority of India and others ...Respondents
Advocate: Mr. Arvind Vashistha, Senior Advocate for the petitioners.
 Mr. Naresh Pant, Advocate for the respondent nos.1 & 2.
 Mr. M.C. Pandey, Additional Advocate General for the State of
 Uttarakhand/respondent nos.3 to 5.

Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
A very peculiar question, though contrary to the records has been
argued by the learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners to the effect that:-
i. When the determination of compensation has been made under
National Highways Act of 1956, it cannot be put to execution under
the Act of 1956 itself, hence the writ petition for the grant of
compensation would be maintainable.
ii. Since there is no dispute with regards to the quantification of the
compensation, or its rival claim, the writ remedy under Article 226 of
the Constitution of India, would be available because of the fact that
the Act of 1956, is silent with regards to the mode to be adopted for
payment of the compensation already determined by the competent
authority.
2. Before answering the aforesaid questions certain basic facts which
are required to be considered by this Court are necessarily required to be dealt
with, which are extracted hereunder:
3. This is a second phase of litigation as the petitioners had earlier
approached the writ court for the grant of relief by way of writ of mandamus for
the payment of compensation of the amount claimed by them to have been
determined after the land was acquired by the respondents, but the same was not

2
remitted. Ultimately, the first phase of litigation, which culminated by way of
Writ Petition (M/S) No.1198 of 2020 Anita Jain vs. Mohan Sah, in which the
petitioners have claimed for the following relief:-
"I. Issue a Writ, Order or direction in the nature of mandamus
to direct the respondents 2 and 3 to pay the compensation along
with interest of acquired land of the petitioners of khasra no.163
area 0.1843 hectare situated at Village, Gajiwali, Pargna And
Tehsil haridwar, District Hridwar to the petitioners as awarded by
respondent no.3 dated 4/5/2019 (Annexure No.12) and approved by
respondent no.2 on 17.09.2019 (Annexure No.14)."
4. The same had been disposed of by the Coordinate Bench of this
Court with direction to the competent authority to take a decision on the
petitioners' application dated 30.12.2019 raising claim for the payment of
compensation, and till the decision was taken status quo, over the property was
directed to be maintained. The relevant part of the judgment is extracted
hereunder:-
"Accordingly, writ petition is disposed of with direction to
the Competent Authority, Land Acquisition (respondent No.3) to
take decision on petitioners' application dated 31.12.2019 as early
as possible, but not later than three weeks from the date of
production of certified copy of this order.
For a period of one week from today, parties shall maintain
status quo over the property in question."
5. In pursuance to the said direction issued by the Coordinate Bench
of this Court, the respondents for the facts, which are going to be disclosed
hereunder, reconducted the entire exercise of determining the payment of
compensation under the National Highway Authority Act of 1956 and had
rejected the claim of the petitioners by the order dated 09.09.2020 and hence,
the present writ petition had been preferred by the petitioners for the following
reliefs:-
"It is therefore most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court
may be pleased to:
(a) Issue a writ order or direction in the nature of certiorari
quashing the order dated 09.09.2020 (Annexure No.25) passed
by the respondent no.3.

3
(b) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of Mandamus
directing the respondents to pay the compensation alongwith
interest of acquired land of the petitioners of Khasra No.163
area 0.1843 hectare situated at Village, Gajiwali, Pargana and
Tehsil Haridwar, District Haridwar to the petitioners as
awarded by respondent no.3 dated 04.05.2019 (Annexure
No.13) and approved by respondent no.2 on 17.09.2019
(Annexure No.14).
(c) Issue any other writ, order or direction which this Hon'be Court
may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the
case.
(d) Award cost of the petition."
6. The brief facts, which are required to be considered in order to
better elucidate upon the questions as raised by the petitioners, in the present
writ petition as detailed above, are that the petitioners have contended that they
are the owners of khasra no.163, lying in Village Gajiwali, Pargana and Tehsil
Haridwar, out of which a land measuring 0.2059 hectares of land, is said to have
been notified under Section 3A of National Highways Act of 1956, for
acquisition of their land for the widening of the National Highway No.74. For
the aforesaid project, a notification was issued on 28.12.2013, which was the
first notification issued, which was later published in Dainik Jagran and other
newspapers of wide circulation, in which the total land of the petitioners which
was proposed to be acquired for widening of NH 74, was included in the
notification as to be 0.2059 hectares. At the time of inspection, prior to the
issuance of notification dated 28.12.2013, the procedure for conducting the
survey under the National Highway Authority Act, was undertaken by the
respondents in pursuance to the provisions contained under Section 3B of the
said Act. It was thereafter they had determined, that the land, which was
acquired for the purpose of the aforesaid project, according to the contention of
the petitioners, the survey and the demarcation proceedings, which were held by
fixing the pillars, a report was thus submitted on 30.06.2016. It was a joint
inspection report, which had been submitted by the authorities, which included
the revenue Sub Inspector, the officials of the National Highway Authority etc.
and it is on the basis of this report of 30.06.2016, the petitioners contend that, in
fact on the submission of the joint inspection report, it was found that the total
land which was actually taken in possession for the aforesaid project, which was
notified on 28.12.2013, the land which was shown to have been taken, as an area

4
of 3902.127 square meters of land, which according to the petitioners and on its
comparative scrutiny, as compared with the notification of 28.12.2013, was
shown to be in excess of about 1843.27 square meters.
7. The petitioners further submitted that the contents of the report of
30.06.2016 and excess acquisition of the land, to the extent of the aforesaid area
i.e. 1843.27 square meters, was a fact, which stood rectified by respondent no.3,
himself by issuance of letter to respondent no.2 on 11.07.2016 and it was further
submitted that in extension to the said communication, the respondent no.3 had
directed the respondent no.2, to pay the excess amount payable towards the land,
which was acquired in excess to the land, which was notified for acquisition.
8. But before the actual process of determining the compensation
could be undertaken in pursuance to the report of 30.06.2016 and the
communication of 11.07.2016, for the second time a joint demarcation
proceedings, were also held alongwith the officials like Special Land
Acquisition Officer (SLAO), Review Officer, and the representatives of
National Highway Authority. In fact, the report submitted thereafter, according
to the petitioners, had rather affirmed contents of the report of 30.06.2016,
fortifying that an excess land of the petitioners had been taken over by the
National Highway Authority.
9. Since there was a deprivation, according to the contention of the
petitioners and because of the fact that an excess land was taken over by the
respondents, without there being a notification issued under Section 3A of
National Highway Authority Act of 1956. The petitioners' made a
representation before the respondents, contending thereof that a fresh
notification may be issued under Section 3A, and after the issuance of the
notification, they may be adequately compensated, for the alleged excess land
acquired, alongwith the compensation payable towards the construction which
were existing on the land, the boundary wall, the electric power fencing and
CCTV cameras etc., which were installed by the petitioners. When no action
was proceeded with in pursuance to the petitioners' representation dated
03.09.2016, the petitioners had contended in the writ petition, that they once
again, had represented their case before the Regional Officer of Uttarakhand,

5
National Highway Authority, on 28.05.2018 and in pursuance to it on the basis
of the recommendations, which were made by the Regional Officer, the
respondent no.2 is said to have written to respondent no.3, on 27.10.2018 calling
upon for issuance of a notification under Section 3A of the Act, for the excess
land which was acquired by the National Highway Authority.
10. The petitioners submitted that in continuation to the earlier
notification of 28.12.2013 and in pursuance to the communication of respondent
no.2 to respondent no.3, which was made on 27.10.2018, in fact the second
notification was issued by the respondents, being the Notification No.4041, New
Delhi, Friday October 12, 2018/ASVINA 20, 1940. The said notification which
was issued in the extraordinary Gazette by the Ministry of Road Transport and
Highways, in fact by the notification of 09.10.2018, it was said to have been
issued in the exercise of powers under Sub Section (1) of Section 3A of National
Highway Authority Act.
11. In relation to the alleged excess land of the petitioners, which was
said to have been acquired by the respondents without issuance of a notification
for the land which was lying in khasra no.163 to the extent of 0.1843 hectares of
land. It is further, the case of the petitioners that on the issuance of the
notification of 09.10.2018, the same was also published in the newspaper on
27.10.2018 in Amar Ujala (Hindi Edition) and Times of India, on the same day,
as per the intention of legislation contained under Section 3G (3) of the National
Highway Authority Act. The counsel for the petitioners submits that since the
notification which was issued for it, only intended to project the acquisition of
the land, hence, the petitioners had raised their grievances by submitting a
representation before respondent no.3 on 29.10.2018, contending thereof, that
the second notification dated 27.10.2018, intending to acquire the excess land as
determined by the reports of 30.06.2016 and the subsequent report, they
submitted, that the determination of the amount of compensation payable to
them should also be inclusive of the various other aspects required for
determination of compensation under Section 3G of the Act, which will be
inclusive of determining the compensation payable to the petitioners at the
commercial value of the land, it should be inclusive of the value of super
structure, which was existing on the land, the permanent pathway, the boundary

6
walls as well as the gates etc. Hence in the objections which were raised by the
petitioners on 29.10.2018, the petitioners claimed a total compensation of a sum
of Rs.75,00,000/-.
12. On the receipt of the complaint of the petitioners dated 29.10.2018,
to the 2nd notification of 27.10.2018, the respondent no.3, issued notices to the
petitioners on 05.11.2018, calling upon them to appear before respondent no.3
on 20.11.2018, for the purposes of determining the adequacy of compensation,
as claimed by the petitioners. In response to the said notice which was issued on
05.11.2018, the petitioners contended that they had appeared before respondent
no.3, on 20.11.2018 and filed their objection wherein they had raised a claim of
revised compensation to the tune of Rs.12,62,22,000/-.
13. Section 3C of the Act, provides for hearing of any person who is
interested for the grant of compensation over the land, which has been acquired
under Section 3A(1) of the Act, and in furtherance to meet the said intention of
the said legislation and further in order to determine the compensation on the
basis of the parameters, which has been laid down under Section 26, of the The
Right to Fair Compensation And Transparency In Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation And Resettlement Act of 2013. The hearing for the same, was
conducted on 27.11.2018.
14. Petitioners submit that the respondent no.2, had reaffirmed the fact,
that excess land of the petitioners has been acquired to the extent of 0.1843
hectares, as notified for acquisition on 27.10.2018 and the publication, which
was made in the Gazette notification of India under Section 3D(2), the
petitioners contend, that since their earlier objections and representations for
determining the adequate compensation under Section 26 of the Act of 2013, has
not been considered in its true perspective, they had to file yet another objection
on 18.02.2019.
15. The petitioners submitted in their representation, that on the
aforesaid objections of the petitioners, as submitted on 20.11.2018 and
18.02.2019, the respondents considered the objections and issued an award on
04.05.2019 whereby, according to the petitioners the award thus determined to

7
be made payable to them was assessed to be a sum payable to the tune of
Rs.6,60,28,660/-. This amount of compensation which was, thus determined in
the award, was published on 04.05.2019 and the petitioners have not raised any
objection to it. Rather they have accepted the propriety of the declaration made
by quantifying the compensation to the said extent and has accepted the award
as determined, to be made payable to the petitioners. In continuation thereto, on
the same day i.e. on 04.05.2019, it is said that the respondent no.3, had written
to respondent no.2 to provide the money to respondent no.3, in order to enable
the respondent no.3, to make the payment of the compensation, which was
determined by the award of 04.05.2019 to the petitioners. The award, thus
published on 04.05.2019, in fact, was placed before the competent authorities of
the National Highway Authority and the competent officer i.e. the Project
Director, PIU, Najibabad, based on the recommendations which were made by
the Award No.2018-2019 dated 04.05.2019, while making reference to the
survey made over the land in question, had approved the award by issuance of
Letter No.NHAI/PIU-NBD/NH-74/33028/Award (HDR)/2016/5998 dated
17.09.2019. Accordingly, as per the said communication, which was made by
respondent no.2, approving the award, which was determined to be made
payable to the petitioners in pursuance to the notification of 27.10.2018, the
National Highway Authority, is said to have discharged their part of liability and
had approved the payment of the amount by depositing the amount as per the
provisions contained under Section 3G (5) of the National Highway Authority
Act of 1956 and under the The Right To Fair Compensation And Transparency
In Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation And Resettlement Act of 2013 directing the
respondents to disburse the compensation by depositing the amount into the
bank accounts of respondent no.3, which was issued from the accounts of the
respondent no.3 standing in the Indus Land Bank, Haridwar, Uttarakhand.
16. On receipt of the said communication of the approval of the award
dated 04.05.2019, as recorded by respondent no.3 on 17.09.2019, the petitioners
contend, that in accordance with the provisions of the Act of 1956, they have
appeared before respondent no.3 for the payment of compensation and have
deposited the Appendix 11 Form CC, alongwith it, the petitioners have also
submitted the affidavits in support of the compensation, the cancel cheques of

8
their accounts standing with the bank, the pan cards, the passbook and all other
relevant documents before respondent no.3 on 23.09.2019.
17. The petitioners have come up with the case, that for the reasons
best known to the respondents and for undisclosed facts and reasons, a third
joint inspection was conducted, after the determination of compensation, by the
award on 04.05.2019 and after its approval on 17.09.2019, which was made by
respondent no.3, who in fact had directed the Tehsildar, vide communication
dated 05.10.2019, to once again conduct a joint inspection of the land and which
was accordingly directed to be conducted on 11.10.2019. In the said inspection,
which was conducted, the petitioners, too are said to have participated in the
proceedings of the joint inspection. When the aforesaid proceedings were being
held, the approved compensation granted by respondent no.2 on 17.09.2019,
when still the compensation was not paid to the petitioners. Henceforth, they
had represented before respondent no.2 to pay the compensation, on 29.11.2019
and on 31.12.2019. The petitioners submitted that they had also represented
before respondent no.3. Apart from praying for the grant of compensation, they
had also submitted that since the award made on 04.05.2019, has not been paid
to the petitioners, despite the deposit being made by the National Highway
Authority, the construction of the road which is being carried by the highway
authorities may be stopped.
18. In a communication which was made by the National Highways
Authority i.e. respondent no.2; herein to the respondent no.3, in fact, respondent
no.3, is said to have passed an order on 04.01.2020, wherein the said Special
Land Acquisition Officer, has written to the Project Director of National
Highway Authority, whereby the representation of the petitioners for the claim
of adequate compensation dated 31.12.2019; was forwarded to be processed as
per law in order to make the payment of compensation. When the same was not
made, the respondent no.3, in order to further proceed to consider the
petitioners' representation of 31.12.2019, had asked the petitioners to submit
certain required documents, in order to facilitate them to press the process of
remittance of compensation and for which respondent no.3, has directed the
petitioners to submit a declaration by way of an affidavit to the effect, that in
case in the future, if there is any defect or discrepancy, which is found to be in

9
the title of the petitioners, the petitioners would undertake to refund the amount,
which is being received by them by way of compensation determined and
approved on 17.09.2019 and the said approval/declaration, was required to be
made by the petitioners by way of Form No.7.
19. The petitioners submitted, that in compliance thereto, the
communication of 04.01.2020, the petitioners have submitted a declaration to
the said effect. But since the amount is not being paid to them, they have yet
again made a representation before the respondents, contending thereof, that
they are reserving their rights to claim an enhanced compensation in future, if
the compensation as determined is not paid to them within the time period,
despite of the recommendations being made on 04.01.2020, by respondent no.3
to respondent no.2.
20. The petitioners have submitted that when they have fulfilled all the
codal formalities as communicated to be complied by the orders of respondent
no.3, the amount is still not being paid, they were forced to approach the writ
court by filing the Writ Petition (M/S) No.1198 of 2020 (as referred above),
which was disposed of on 12.08.2020 (the extract of the judgment which is
quoted above). The petitioners contended that despite, there being an order
passed by the Coordinate Bench of this Court on 12.08.2020, in fact, the
respondents, who were restrained from taking over possession, because there
was an order of status quo passed and because of the fact that no compensation
was paid; till the date of passing of the order by the Coordinate Bench of this
Court. The petitioners grievances are that, despite the issuance of notification of
acquisition and determination of compensation by way of an award, they submit
that, on the contrary the respondent no.2 has acted with a deliberate and ill
intention, contrary to the order of 12.08.2020, which was passed by this Court
by issuing a correspondence to respondent no.3 on 07.09.2020, to take
possession of the land of the petitioners with the help of police.
21. The petitioners contend that this direction which had been issued on
07.09.2020, was contemptuous in nature, as being apparently in contravention to
the earlier judgment of 12.08.2020. The petitioners further submitted that, in
light of the consequential and sequel inspections, which were conducted, in

10
itself showed, that the survey being made as per the provisions of the Act of
1956, after hearing of the objection of the petitioners, when the amount was not
determined, the petitioners submitted in their pleadings that the respondents in
order to delay the payment of compensation, had once again directed to conduct
an inspection in compliance of same order, which was said to have been passed
by the Divisional Forest Officer; for yet again a demarcation of the Northern
side of the land, which was proposed to be acquired by the Revenue
Department.
22. The grievances of the petitioners remained unredressed and hence
according to the contentions raised by the petitioners in the writ petition, that
while application of the release of compensation was pending consideration
before the Special Land Acquisition Officer/(SLAO) despite, having been
published the award, the respondents for the reasons best known to them are
said to have again directed for conducting the resurvey and the petitioners have
raised their grievance that the said direction, which was issued, was uncalled for,
particularly in light of the fact that the process of determination of the
compensation had stood culminated in the light of the provisions contained
under Section 3G of the Act of 1956. Hence, there did not exist at all a need to
conduct a resurvey, as intended to be conducted on 05.09.2020 and that the
entire process in itself was bad because the petitioners, were not given a prior
notice, and as per the so called reports, which are said to have been submitted by
resurvey team which had conducted the survey, were bad because no fixed point
was ever determined by the survey team and even the Revenue Team in their
presence and had not considered the description of the property, which was
lying to Khasra No.163 as it was raised in the Sajara.
23. The petitioners contend, that since there was no controversy as such
left for the determination of the compensation, because of the issuance of second
notification on 27.10.2018 and the determination of the compensation, which
was made by an award of 04.05.2019 and its ultimate approval which had been
granted by respondent no.3 on 17.09.2019, coupled with the fact that when the
neighbourers of the property also did not raise any objection whatsoever
regarding the area of the land acquired by the petitioners, despite of the fact that
the adjoining land tenure holder i.e. Mr. Madan Harmilap, also had his land

11
acquired lying in Khasra No.164, he too also did not raise any objection against
the acquisition of the excess land of the petitioners, acquired subsequently by
the respondents. The petitioners contend, that since there was no dispute of the
area acquired qua the other surrounding tenure holders; hence, they were
entitled to be paid with the compensation.
24. It is at this stage that the actual controversy started germinating.
The petitioners in the entire body of the writ petition, up to the stage of conduct
of the third resurvey on 05.09.2020, had always portrayed as if that after the
approval of the award made on 17.09.2019, which was granted by respondent
no.2, the image which was created by the petitioners in their pleadings and
arguments too, was that as if there was no dispute at all which could create any
impediment, for the payment of compensation and hence, the respondents were
bound by the direction, which was issued by the Coordinate Bench by the
judgment of 12.08.2020. However, the petitioners contended that despite of
having submitted their objections to the respondents regarding the resurvey,
being conducted on 05.09.2020, by filing their objections on 08.09.2020, which
was supported with the Sajra map of Gurukul Kangari and the other adjoining
land including the depiction of the pillars, which were fixed by the survey team.
The petitioners contended, that when there had been a direction by respondent
no.3 on the petitioners' application dated 13.12.2019, the amount of
compensation ought to have been remitted to them.
25. When this entire act, even after the judgment of 12.08.2020, was
not conducted as per law, the petitioners submitted that they filed a contempt
petition, being Contempt Petition No.352 of 2020 and Contempt Petition
No.347 of 2020 (as referred in para 45 of the writ petition), however, the
aforesaid Contempt Petition was said to have been closed as withdrawn by the
petitioners by the order of 23.09.2020, but the petitioners' had placed only one
of the orders i.e. of 23.09.2020, on records of the writ petition in relation to the
Contempt Petition No.352 of 2020, but what had happened to the Contempt
Petition No.347 of 2020, which was described by the petitioners in para 45 of
the writ petition, no details have been forthcoming in the pleadings which were
raised in writ petition.

12
26. What is important here is that admittedly, according to the
contentions raised by the petitioners in para 46 of the writ petition, in fact it is
the actual dispute which emerges for consideration. In fact, according to the plea
of para 46 of the writ petition, which would show, that as against the
determination of the award made on 04.05.2019, there was a complaint which
was submitted by one Mr. Dinesh Kumar, resident of Plot No.112 Shivratan
City, Noida, who had submitted a complaint before the SLAO, wherein he has
raised his objection, as against the determination of the compensation made in
favour of the petitioners. Taking cognizance of the aforesaid complaint of Mr.
Dinesh Kumar, pertaining to the fixation of the boundary pillars of the two
villages Gajiwali and Kangri and fixation of the points for the purposes of
demarcation of the land by the Revenue Department, the objection of Mr.
Dinesh Kumar as submitted to 09.09.2019, he controverted on an issue of the
entitlement of the petitioners for the grant of compensation.
27. On this complaint, rather the petitioners were called upon to submit
their reply, which was responded, by the petitioners, by merely submitting, that
the complaint is fictitious and unsustainable and the complainant Dinesh Kumar,
has got no right of any nature whatsoever over the excess land, which was
acquired of khasra no.163 which was a subject matter of acquisition as notified
on 27.10.2018 under Section 3A (1). They further submitted that there is no
such person, who has got right in any manner, whatsoever over the land for
which the petitioners were claiming compensation.
28 From the pleading of para 46 and 47 of the writ petition, which are
extracted hereunder:-
"46. That the impugned order shows that a complaint dated
09.09.2019 from one Dinesh Kumar resident of plot no.112,
Shivratan City, Noida Nagar, near Oxford Roshanabad, Haridwar
was received where the complainant highlighted certain
discrepancy. It is submitted that S.L.A.O./C.A.L.A. herself issued
notices to the alleged complainant and the petitioner. The petitioner
responded but there was no response from the alleged complainant.
As a matter of fact the alleged complainant namely Dinesh Kumar
is fictitious person and no such person exist. The alleged complaint
has been fabricated only for the purposes of arbitrary exercise of
powers.

13
47. That the boundary pillar of the 2 villages namely Gajiwali
and Kangri is the fixed point which has been admittedly exist to the
revenue department as well as forest department in the survey
however, the aforementioned fixed point was not at all considered
and the survey have been carried out treating 2 chak roads as fixed
point while the respondent herself has disputed 'Sajra map'".
29. This Court is of the view that following dispute has emerged:-
i. That it is not an undisputed amount of an award, which the petitioners
could be said to be entitled to receive by an award of 04.05.2019 as it stood
approved on 17.09.2019.
ii. That, there was an objection raised by one Mr. Dinesh Kumar, which in
that eventuality of filling of an objection and the resulting into issuance of the
notice to the petitioners would in itself make the award to be disputed.
iii. That, in view of the pleadings raised in para 46 of the writ petition, itself
with all genuineness and fairness at the hands of the petitioners, it was expected
that the petitioners ought to have impleaded Mr. Dinesh Kumar, as a party to the
writ petition, so that he may raise his contentions, about the entitlement of the
petitioners for the grant of compensation having not done so, the writ petition
itself become would be defective because of the non-joinder of the necessary
party.
30. Hence it cannot be said and be accepted too by this Court, and as
contended by the petitioners in the writ petition, that the amount of award
determined by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, was an undisputed amount
for which a writ of mandamus would lie.
31. Its upon this backdrop, when the writ petition was instituted on
25.09.2020, the Coordinate Bench of this Court, had called upon the counter
affidavit to be filed by the respondents by virtue of its order dated 05.10.2020.
In response to it, the respondents had filed their respective counter affidavits.
The respondent nos.1 and 2 had filed their counter on 01.11.2020, wherein the
respondent nos.1 and 2, had submitted that the claim which has been raised by
the petitioners for grant of compensation, may not be sustainable in the eyes of

14
law for the reason being, that there was an apparent dispute, which was raised
by the complainant Mr. Deepak Kumar, about the petitioners' entitlement to
receive the compensation, but principally the respondent nos.1 and 2 i.e. the
representative of the National Highway Authority of India, had submitted, that
since after the determination of the compensation, they have already remitted
the amount into the accounts of the respondent no.3, as per the provisions
contained under Section 3H of the National Highway Authority Act of 1956 and
particularly a reference may be had to para 16 of their counter affidavit,
wherein the respondents authorities have submitted that respondent nos.1 and 2
have acted in accordance with Section 3E of the Act and possession has been
taken over after depositing the amount under Section 3H. The respondent nos.1
& 2 have submitted that they do not have any dispute as such apparent, from the
records of the writ petition, for the payment of compensation.
32. On the other hand, the principal counter affidavit, which has been
filed by respondent no.3 on 07.11.2020, they had submitted that in fact the NH-74 (which was later on renamed as NH-34) they have submitted, that petitioners
would not be entitled for the grant of the compensation, because of the fact that
there was a dispute which had arisen because of the objection which had been
submitted by one Mr. Dinesh Kumar, for the grant of compensation to the
petitioners. Hence, while considering the objections submitted by the
respondents, the respondents had rejected the claim of the petitioners by an
order of 09.09.2020 and hence, they submitted that the Writ Petition No.1195
of 2020 (M/S), which was filed by the petitioners, the writ petition was liable to
be dismissed.
33. At this stage itself, the determination of the propriety of the order
which was passed by respondents on 09.09.2020, becomes eminent to be
considered by this court. The Special Land Acquisition Officer, while
considering the claim of the petitioners, raised by the representation dated
31.12.2019 and the objection raised thereto, to it by Mr. Dinesh Kumar, on his
Complaint No.1345 dated 24.09.2019, had rejected the claim of the petitioners
by the impugned order dated 09.09.2020, which has been put to challenge in the
present writ petition.

15
34. The respondent no.3 further in the counter affidavit had submitted
that the petitioners would not be entitled for the payment of compensation for
the additional land, which has been acquired for the reason being that so far as
the land measuring 0.0259 hectares, is concerned, the total amount, which was
determined to be paid, has already been received by the petitioners and it was in
fact rather on the complaint submitted by Mr. Dinesh Kumar, that the District

inter alia on the ground that the issues stood determined in terms of

relying or on the basis of the declarations made by the appellants
in terms of Form F. However, the reassessment proceeding was
completed relying upon the provisions contained in Section 16 of
the State Act read with Section 9(2) of the Central Act as also in
terms of the decision of this Court in Sahney Steel & Press Works
Ltd. v. CTO, Consequent to the said order the sales of the Regional
Sales Offices in relation to the deliveries made to the State
Transport Undertakings of other States were reassessed. Penalty
for non-disclosure of the turnover as taxable sales in terms of

28
Section 16(2) of the State Act read with Section 9(2) of the Central
Act was also imposed. Similar show cause notices were issued in
relation to other assessment years also."
52. The Hon'ble Apex Court in yet another judgment which is reported
in (2019) 9 Supreme Court Cases 304, Union of India and Another vs.
Tarsem Singh and Others, though it was slightly dealing with a different
prospective, from the view point that the payment under the proceedings of
acquisition, which are held under National Highway Authority Act of 1956, was
held to be arbitrary in the light of the provisions contained under Article 14 of
the Constitution of India; but for the purposes of the present case, only para 45
of the said judgment would be relevant which is extracted hereunder:-
"45. Insofar as easementary rights under the Land Acquisition
Act are concerned, three Sections are relevant and need to be
quoted:
"3. Definitions.- In this Act, unless there is something
repugnant in the subject or context,--
(b) the expression "person interested" includes all persons claiming
an interest in compensation to be made on account of the
acquisition of land under this Act; and a person shall be deemed to
be interested in land if he is interested in an easement affecting the
land;
9. Notice to persons interested.-- (1) The Collector shall then cause
public notice to be given at convenient places on or near the land
to be taken, stating that the Government intends to take possession
of the land, and that claims to compensation for all interests in
such land may be made to him.
(2) Such notice shall state the particulars of the land so needed,
and shall require all persons interested in the land to appear
personally or by agent before the Collector at a time and place
therein mentioned (such time not being earlier than fifteen days
after the date of publication of the notice), and to state the nature of
their respective interests in the land and the amount and
particulars of their claims to compensation for such interests, and
their objections (if any) to the measurements made Under Section
8. The Collector may in any case require such statement to be made
in writing and signed by the party or his agent.
(3) The Collector shall also serve notice to the same effect on the
occupier (if any) of such land and on all such persons known or
believed to be interested therein, or to be entitled to act for persons
so interested, as reside or have agents authorised to receive service
on their behalf, within the revenue district in which the land is
situate.
(4) In case any person so interested resides elsewhere, and has no
such agent the notice shall be sent to him by post in a letter
addressed to him at his last known residence, address or place of

29
business and registered Under Sections 28 and 29 of the Indian
Post Office Act, 1898 (6 of 1898).
31. Payment of compensation or deposit of same in Court.--
(1) On making an award Under Section 11, the Collector shall
tender payment of the compensation awarded by him to the persons
interested entitled thereto according to the award, and shall pay it
to them unless prevented by some one or more of the contingencies
mentioned in the next Sub-section.
A reading of these Sections shows that a person who is
interested in an easement affecting land can claim compensation
therefor under the aforesaid provisions of the Land Acquisition Act.
Under both the Land Acquisition Act and the National Highways
Act, such claims have to be proved in accordance with law, the
difference being that under the Land Acquisition Act actuals are
payable, whereas under the National Highways Act, a fixed amount
of 10% of the amount determined by the competent authority is
payable. It is, therefore, wholly incorrect to state that extra
amounts are payable to the owner under the National Highways
Act, which are not so payable under the Land Acquisition Act. Also,
both Acts contemplate payment of compensation to persons whose
easementary rights have been affected by the acquisition. In any
event, this contention cannot possibly answer non-payment of
solatium and interest under the National Highways Act, which has
been dealt with in extenso in this judgment."
53. Rather in fact, it had laid down that both the Land Acquisition Act,
as well as the National Highway Authority Act 1956, contemplate a payment of
compensation where there is a breach or infringement of an easementry right of
a person, who under law is proved to be the owner of the property. The relevant
para 45, which has been extracted above, in fact the entitlement, for the
determination of a right has to be done by the competent authority under Section
3A in relation to the land acquired under Section 3A(1) and its determination
has been exclusively fallen to be kept within the ambit of Section 3G (5) and not
by way of any other procedural exception particularly, when it is contemplated
under a special Act and hence, since the Act itself has been given an overriding
effect in the light of the reasoning given in para 45 and when it is dealing with
the person affected, it would obviously mean that it would include the
determination of compensation under the provisions of the Arbitration and
Conciliation Act of 1996, which could be enforceable under the provisions of
the Act itself, and not otherwise.
54. The Division Bench of Madras High Court in a judgment rendered
in W.A. (MD) Nos. 1928 to 1931 of 2011 and M.P. (MD) No.01 of 2011 in

30
W.A. (MD) Nos.1930 and 1931 of 2019 C. Gopinath vs. District Collector
and Others as rendered on 14.12.2015, it has held that Section 3H (4) of the
National Highway Authority Act, is only an enabling provisions, therefore, once
the satisfaction has been recorded by the competent authority under Section 3A
for the disbursement of the amount, to a person who is making his claim, the
issue of entitlement could only be decided by the mechanism provided under
Section 3G of the Act and this is what has been contemplated in paragraphs 16,
17 and 18 of the said judgment, which is extracted hereunder:-
16. Section 3-G of the National Highways Act, 1956 contains an
elaborate procedure for the determination of the compensation
payable to the owners of the land, which is acquired by the
Competent Authority under the National Highways Act, 1956. After
the determination of the amount under Section 3-G, the Central
Government is obliged under Section 3-H to deposit the amount so
determined in a manner as prescribed by Rules with the Competent
Authority. Sub-section (2) of Section 3-H obliges the Competent
Authority to pay the amount immediately after it is so deposited
under sub- section (1). What happens when several persons stake a
claim for disbursement of the compensation, is prescribed under
sub-section (3) of Section 3-H. When the claims so made by several
persons lead to a dispute, the same has to be resolved in terms of
the provisions of sub-section (4) of Section 3-H. Since the
determination of the question raised in these appeals revolves
around sub-sections (3) and (4) of Section 3-H, they are extracted
as follows: "3-H. Deposit and payment of amount. -
***** (3) Where several persons claim to be interested in the
amount deposited under sub-section (1), the competent authority
shall determine the persons who in its opinion are entitled to
receive the amount payable to each of them.
(4) If any dispute arises as to the apportionment of the amount or
any part thereof or to any person to whom the same or any part
thereof is payable, the competent authority shall refer the dispute to
the decision of the principal Civil Court of original jurisdiction
within the limits of whose jurisdiction the land is situated."
17. A careful reading of sub-sections (3) and (4) of Section 3-
H would show that the statute uses the expression "claim" in sub-section (3) and the expression "dispute" in sub-section (4).
Therefore the Competent Authority is not entitled to adjudicate
upon the disputes. If the claims are made by several persons,
without any inter se dispute among themselves, the Competent
Authority is entitled to disburse the amount under sub-section (3).
The entitlement of the Competent Authority to determine the
persons under sub- section (3), is of a limited nature, but whenever
a dispute arises, the Competent Authority is obliged to refer the
dispute to the decision of the Principal Court of civil jurisdiction. If

31
such an interpretation is not given, the Competent Authority may
arrogate to himself the powers of the civil Court to adjudicate upon
civil disputes. Therefore we are of the considered view that the
learned Judge was not right in thinking that sub- section (4)
of Section 3-H is merely an enabling provision and that the parties
could go to the civil Court independently. Such a view would confer
powers which are not available and which should not be made
available to the Competent Authority to adjudicate civil disputes
relating to disbursement of compensation.
18. Therefore all the appeals are allowed. The order of the learned
Judge is set aside and the Competent Authority is directed to refer
the dispute to the appropriate civil Court, as per sub-section (4)
of Section 3-H within a period of four weeks from the date of
receipt of a copy of this judgment. The competent Court shall issue
notice to all the parties and adjudicate upon the dispute after
adequate opportunities possibly within a period of six months
thereafter. The Competent Authority appears to have drawn a
cheque in favour of Mani, but did not hand it over to him. The
Competent Authority shall deposit the money to the credit of the
civil Court to which a reference is made. Along with the request for
reference to be made by the Competent Authority, he shall deposit
the money into that Court and the Court concerned shall keep the
money in a Fixed Deposit until the disposal of the dispute. No costs.
Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petitions are closed."
55. Hence, in view of the said judgment of the Division Bench of the
Madras High Court, the petitioners' claim would not fall to be within the scope
of consideration under Article 226 of the Constitution of India. There are other
judgments for example, (2013) AIR (Kar) 163 B.L Sridhar and Others vs.
B.R. Pathi and Others, where almost an identical view has been taken by the
Karnataka High Court in paras 5 and 8 of the said judgment, which is extracted
hereunder:-
"5. The only point to be considered in this appeal is considering the
actual dispute between the parties, whether Sub-section (3) of
Section 3-H of the National Highways Act or Sub-section (4) of
Section 3-H of the National Highways Act, is applicable in order to
find out whether the order of the Learned Single Judge suffers from
any error.
 *******
8. We could have appreciated the arguments of the learned counsel
for the appellants that Special Land Acquisition Officer was
justified in invoking Subsection (3) of Section 3-H of the Act,
provided there was no dispute between the appellants and the
respondent in regard to the extent of land held by each of them.
If there is no dispute in regard to the extent of land held by
each of them, based on their claim, amount could have

32
disbursed by invoking Subsection (3) of Section 3-H. On the
contrary, the actual dispute in question is whether the
appellants are the owners of the entire extent of 5 guntas and
whether the Writ Petitioner is also having a share out of 5
guntas. It is nothing but a title dispute. Such disputes cannot be
adjudicated under Sub-section (3) of Section 3-H and it falls
within the provision of Sub-section (4)."
56. Where the mechanism of adjudication has been itself included in a
self contained special statute, which is covered by Schedule 7th Schedule of the
Constitution and coupled with the fact that since the applicability of the General
Law of the Land Acquisition, has been ousted to be made applicable, the
determination has to be exclusively made under Section 3G of the Special Act
and merely because of the deposit of the amount under Section 3H, that in itself
cannot be made payable without a determination made, and particularly where
there is a complaint raised by the private person about a right which has to be
determined by the competent authority.
57. To sum up as to what has been determined above, this Court
concludes as under:-
i. The word "determination" without a reference under Section 3G and
without there being an award by an Arbitration under Section 3G (5),
would not exclude the applicability of execution proceedings under the
Arbitration Act of 1996, which has been exclusively made applicable
in the light of the provision contained under Section 3G (6). Thus, the
recourse made available to the petitioners to enforce an award would
be to file an appropriate proceedings under Section 36 of the
Arbitration and Conciliation Act of 1996, for the enforcement of a
disputed claim of compensation.
ii. This Court after dealing with the controversy is of the view that the
present case, would not fall within the parameters of writ of mandamus
under Article 226 of the Constitution of India of 1950, particularly
when there is a controversy raised by a private person pertaining to the
determination of compensation made on 04.05.2019, which would
have an element of civil rights too, in relation to the land. This, in
itself would make the controversy referable to an Arbitrator under

33
Section 3G (5). Henceforth, a writ of mandamus would not lie because
the amount is disputed, the claim is disputed and until the same is
adjudicated by the mechanism provided under the Special Act, itself
no mandamus can be issued.
iii. The writ under Article 226 of Constitution, in itself would be bad due
to the non-joinder of necessary parties, particularly when the
petitioners are conscious of the fact, that a private person has already
raised an objection about the claim to be determined by the Arbitrator.
Hence, the objector Mr. Dinesh Kumar, should have been made as a
party to the writ petition because issuance of any writ of mandamus in
his absence would obviously have a prejudicial effect to the rights and
interest of the objector.
iv. This Court is of the view that if the reasoning given in the impugned
order dated 09.09.2020, are taken into consideration, when the
resurvey was conducted on 05.09.2020, it was rather on the complaint
of the private respondents submitted on 25.05.2019, where in fact, it
was found that the petitioners were in possession of excess of the land,
then to what they were actually entitled to as per law and the entries
made in the revenue record, which required a determination of facts,
by appreciating the evidence by the authority created under the Act
itself i.e. under Section 3G (5) and the same cannot be undertaken by
way of writ of mandamus.
v. On an ultimate conclusion, I am of the view that the fine distinction
which was attempted to be carved out by the counsel for the petitioners
with regards to the terms, "determination and award" in fact literally,
is more or less a para materia provision and if at all it has to be, it has
to extracted from the principles of Code of Civil Procedure 1908, that
"determination would be a judgment", as defined under Sub Section
(9) of Section 2 of the Code, and "award would be a decree", as
defined under Sub Section (2) of Section 2 of C.P.C. 1908. In fact the
award would be a final expression made of a judgment by virtue of a
determination, which would be enforceable as a decree under Section
36 of the Act. But for the reasons given above, even this remedy of
Section 36, at this stage would not be available to the petitioners, until
and unless they get their rights determined qua the private objections

34
by invoking the provisions contained under Section 3G (5), where
there is an objection to the right, there is an objection of the area
acquired, where there is an objection of the entitlement of the
petitioners to receive the compensation.
58. Accordingly, for the reasons given above, the writ petition fails and
the same is accordingly, dismissed.
